title: RegelRecht Execution Trace Schema v0.5.9
description: An execution trace: the tree of steps an engine took to reach a result, addressable and anchored to the provisions the steps came from (RFC-039). Versioned independently of the law schema, like the note sidecar. A conformant engine produces this document; the box-drawing text rendering is a presentation of it and is not part of the contract.

trace_version.description: Version of this trace format. Incremented when a change would break a consumer; new optional fields do not.

root.description: The outermost step, which is the evaluation the caller asked for.

TraceNode.description: One step. Children are the nested steps it took, in the order it took them.

node_type.description: What kind of step this is.

name.description: What the step was about: a value name, an operation, or '<law>#<output>' for a cross-law reference. Not an address: two steps in different laws can share a name. Use node_id to address a step and uri to address the value.

result.description: The value the step produced. Absent when the step produced none. The three absences are distinct (RFC-036): null is a value the data asserts, an unknown names the facts nobody has, and an omitted result means the step yielded nothing.

resolve_type.description: For a resolve step, where the value was looked up. Repeated inside source.kind for a consumer reading only source.

children.description: Nested steps, in execution order. Omitted when there are none.

node_id.description: Address of this step within this trace: the chain of child indices from the root. The root is 'n', its first child 'n0', that child's third child 'n0.2'. Unique within a trace and identical for the same inputs, so a fixture can pin one and a URL fragment can point at one. It addresses a position in this trace, not an identity across traces: two evaluations whose trees differ in shape, for instance because one reused a memoized cross-law result, address the same work differently.

anchor.description: Where the engine was when it took this step. Reported whenever the engine knows the provision, independent of what the law document happens to cite.

legal_basis.description: The citation the law document declares for the element at yaml_path, reported as written. Absent when that element declares none, which is not the same as the engine not knowing where it was: compare anchor. An engine that does not retain the law document reports none.

yaml_path.description: Address of the element within the law document, as a dotted path whose segments are keys, and for a list item the value of its 'output', 'name' or 'number' rather than its index: 'articles.2.machine_readable.execution.actions.hoogte_zorgtoeslag.value.values.1'. A dot inside a label is written as an underscore, so article '2.34' is addressed as '2_34'. Addresses an element that has no name of its own, such as one branch of a nested operation, which no regelrecht:// URI can name.

uri.description: Address of the value this step denotes, as a regelrecht:// URI. Present on a step that denotes a value rather than a piece of work.

source.description: Where a resolved value came from, in fields rather than in prose.

type_spec.description: Unit and precision of 'result', so a consumer can present 209692 as an amount in euros. Present when the value's declaration carries one, which parameters, inputs, outputs and definitions do; an intermediate operation result has no declaration and therefore no type_spec.

duration_us.description: How long the step took, in microseconds. Optional, and absent wherever an engine does not measure it, so no consumer may depend on it.

message.description: A line about this step for a person reading the trace in a terminal. Presentational: the wording is not a contract, it may be phrased in any language, and parsing it is a defect. Every fact it states is available in a field.

LegalAnchor.description: A reference to a provision. Same shape as the law schema's legal_basis, so the engine's account of where it was and the document's own citation are comparable rather than two dialects.

law_id.description: Law identifier as the corpus knows it, e.g. 'wet_op_de_zorgtoeslag'.

law.description: Law name as cited in prose, e.g. 'Wet op de zorgtoeslag'.

law_uuid.description: Stable uuid of the law version, when it has one.

article.description: Article number as the law writes it: '2', '1a', 'B1'.

sentence.description: Sentence, for a reference finer than a lid.

url.description: Link to the provision on wetten.overheid.nl.

valid_from.description: valid_from of the law version this anchor points into.

explanation.description: The modeller's note on how the element relates to the text. Occurs on a legal_basis and never on an anchor: an engine has no such note to report.

ValueSource.description: Where a resolved value came from (RFC-039), replacing what a consumer used to read out of 'message'.

kind.description: How the value was resolved. Same vocabulary as resolve_type.

provider.description: The registered data source that held the value, which is the organisation keeping the register. Absent for a kind that has no provider, such as a definition in the law itself.

scope.description: The law a scoped data source was registered for. Absent when the source is global.

TypeSpec.description: Unit and precision of a value, as the law schema declares them (RFC-023).

unit.description: Unit of measurement, e.g. 'eurocent', 'ratio', 'days'. A label, never a computational constraint.

precision.description: Number of decimal places for the value in its own unit.
